fields.Front: Define 'relationship' (ER model).
fields.Back: A named grouping of entities; an association among two or more entities, e.g. Employee WORKS FOR Department.

fields.Front: What is a relationship set / relationship type formally?
fields.Back: A relationship type R among entity types E1..En is a set of relationship instances ri, each associating n entities (e1..en) with ej from Ej; i.e. a mathematical relation on E1..En. Example: ('Reid','CS3319') in the set of (Prof, Course).

fields.Text: In Chen notation a relationship type is a {{c1::diamond}} with lines to each entity; a relationship attribute is an {{c2::oval attached to the diamond}}.

fields.Front: What is the degree of a relationship?
fields.Back: The number of entity types participating in it: unary (1), binary (2), ternary (3).

fields.Front: Define a unary (recursive) relationship and give an example.
fields.Back: An entity of one entity type has a relationship with other entities of the same entity type; e.g. Employee MANAGES/SUPERVISES Employee.

fields.Front: Define a binary relationship and give the slide example.
fields.Back: A relationship between two entity types; e.g. Student TAKES Course (with relationship attribute Grade).

fields.Front: Define a ternary relationship and give the slide example.
fields.Back: A relationship among three entity types; e.g. Supplier SUPPLIES Part to Project, with relationship attribute Quantity.

fields.Text: In the slide's ternary example, the entities are {{c1::Supplier, Part and Project}} and the relationship Supply has the attribute {{c2::Quantity}}.

fields.Front: What is an attribute on a relationship? Give the Student-takes-Course example.
fields.Back: An attribute describing the relationship instance itself, not either entity: Grade belongs to the (student, course) pair.

fields.Front: Define 'cardinality ratio'.
fields.Back: The number of relationship instances an entity can participate in; the three common ones are 1:1, 1:N (many-to-one) and M:N.

fields.Front: Give the case-study example of a one-to-one relationship.
fields.Back: Employee MANAGES Department.

fields.Front: Give the case-study example of a many-to-one relationship.
fields.Back: Employee WORKS FOR Department.

fields.Front: Give the case-study example of a many-to-many relationship.
fields.Back: Employee WORKS ON Project.

fields.Text: Cardinality examples: 1:1 = Employee {{c1::MANAGES}} Department; N:1 = Employee {{c2::WORKS FOR}} Department; M:N = Employee {{c3::WORKS ON}} Project.
Man BIOLOGICALLY FATHERS Child has cardinality {{c1::one to many}}.
The speaker notes' example of a many-to-many relationship is {{c1::Sister HAS Brother}}; in the video the instructor uses {{c2::Student takes Course}}.

fields.Front: On a Chen diagram, where is the cardinality letter (1, M, N) written for Employee WORKS FOR Department?
fields.Back: N (many) next to EMPLOYEE and 1 next to DEPARTMENT: many employees work for one department.

fields.Front: Draw 'An artist paints paintings' (Chen): cardinality on each side?
fields.Back: ARTIST (1) --- paints --- (M) PAINTING.

fields.Front: Draw 'A person owns pets' (Chen): cardinality on each side?
fields.Back: PERSON (1) --- owns --- (M) PET.

fields.Front: How are 'currently married to' and 'was married to' between WOMAN and MAN modelled?
fields.Back: Currently Married To: 1:1 with attribute Wedding Date. Was Married To: M:N with attributes Wedding Date and Marriage End Date.

fields.Front: In the WORKS FOR instance diagram (Laura, Roberto, e3, e4 / Computer Science, Math, English), how many entity types participate?
fields.Back: Two (Employee and Department): it is a binary relationship.

fields.Front: Explain the instructor's 'Laura and CS3319' relationship example.
fields.Back: An instance of the Prof entity and an instance of the Course entity grouped together; the relationship set is the ordered pair (Laura, CS3319); the relationship type is TEACHES.

fields.Front: Homer Simpson (student 15) got 89. Why can Grade not be an attribute of STUDENT, and why not of COURSE?
fields.Back: On STUDENT you cannot tell which course the 89 was for (CS2210 or CS3319); on COURSE you cannot tell which student earned it. Grade belongs to the (student, course) pair, so it goes on the TAKES relationship.

fields.Text: An attribute on a relationship describes the {{c1::combination of the entities together}}, not either entity on its own.

fields.Front: How does the instructor explain Quantity on the ternary Supply relationship?
fields.Back: 'Maybe we're supplying seven of these parts from this supplier for this project': the quantity depends on all three of supplier, part and project.

fields.Front: Describe the instructor's 'could' technique for finding a cardinality ratio.
fields.Back: Take one instance of the left entity and ask 'an X could relate to how many Y?'; write the answer beside Y. Then look at it backwards from Y and write that answer beside X. Use 'could', not 'must': cardinality is the maximum.

fields.Text: For cardinality use the word {{c1::could}}; the words {{c2::must / every}} belong to participation.

fields.Front: Why did the instructor write 'Man BIOLOGICALLY fathers Child'?
fields.Back: Because step-fathers or adoptive fathers would change the cardinality; biologically, a child has exactly one father and a man can father many children (1:N).

fields.Front: Person OWNS Pet: how does the instructor answer the objection that a whole family owns the pet?
fields.Back: In a vet's database you keep one person's name on file, so a pet is owned by one person (1:N). Context decides.

fields.Text: 'In the great province of Ontario' a woman can currently be married to at most {{c1::one}} man, so Currently Married To is {{c2::1:1}}; Was Married To is {{c3::M:N}}.

fields.Front: Why does the instructor label a many-to-many relationship M and N rather than M and M?
fields.Back: So you do not think the two 'many' values must be equal (a woman with five ex-husbands does not mean each man had five ex-wives). M and M is also allowed.

fields.Front: How would 'a woman is currently married to a woman' be drawn?
fields.Back: As a unary (recursive) relationship on WOMAN, 1:1 (and Was Married To as unary M:N).

fields.Text: The case-study relationship that is 'not one of the obvious ones' is the unary {{c1::SUPERVISES}}: an employee supervises many employees and is supervised by {{c2::one}} boss.

fields.Front: What assumption did the instructor make so that a dependent belongs to only one employee?
fields.Back: That no married couples work at the company; otherwise a child could be the dependent of two employees.

fields.Front: List the learning objectives of Video 6 (relationships).
fields.Back: Define relationship, cardinality, unary, binary, ternary, one-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many; use the correct symbols to draw relationships on an ER diagram; identify attributes that should be on relationships.
